SL-GP could bind to IL-1 beta treated HUVEC, and the binding was inhibited by anti-E-selectin and anti-SLeA monoclonal antibodies.
The binding of colorectal cancer cells, LS 180, to HUVEC was assayed in the presence of SL-GP, oligosaccharides prepared from SL-GP and human milk SLeA hexasaccharide.
SL-GP inhibited the binding most effectively, whereas equivalent amounts of the SL-GP oligosaccharides and milk SLeA hexasaccharide inhibited it only slightly.
These results constitute direct evidence that a unique arrangement of SLeA antigens on the polypeptide chain, probably a cluster, is essential for the binding to E-selectin.
